answer: Persistent Resource Pin. Each identity must hold a dedicated slice of scarce shared storage—say a jetty buffer or bandwidth reservation—for the full epoch. Honesty keeps the pin small because real agents reuse one contiguous block; a clone needs its own freshly allocated region, so cost scales linearly with identity count rather than amortizing across a plume of aliases. Release requires proof the prior slice was fully consumed, which cloned agents can't fake without paying twice. The result is a vine of identities where each new node carries a full unshared rent.
